Una función $z = f(x, y)$ da una altura: A function $z = f(x, y)$ gives a height $z$ to each point $(x, y)$ of the plane; the set of points $(x, y, f(x, y))$ is a surface. A level curve is the set of points of the plane where $f(x, y) = k$: it is what a topographic map draws (curves very close together mean a steep slope).
$f_{x}$ es la derivada respecto de x con: $f_{x}$ is the derivative with respect to x with y constant, and $f_{y}$ the other way round. The gradient $∇f = (f_{x}, f_{y})$ points where $f$ grows fastest, its magnitude $|∇f|$ is that maximum slope and it is always perpendicular to the level curve through the point.
Su normal es $n = (f_{x}, f_{y}, −1)$. C: Its normal is $n = (f_{x}, f_{y}, −1)$. Near the point the surface almost coincides with the plane, so $f(x, y) ≈ $ the height of the plane: it is the linear approximation, and the error grows as you move away.
$D_{u} f = ∇f · u = f_{x} u_{x} + f_{y}: $D_{u} f = ∇f · u = f_{x} u_{x} + f_{y} u_{y}$,   with $|u| = 1$
Es la pendiente de la superficie al avan: It is the slope of the surface when moving in the direction $u$. It takes its maximum value, $|∇f|$, if $u$ goes with the gradient, its minimum, $−|∇f|$, in the opposite direction, and zero along the level curve.
Los extremos no siempre cumplen $f_{x} =: Extrema do not always satisfy $f_{x} = f_{y} = 0$: the cone $z = √{x^2 + y^2}$ has its minimum at the vertex, where there are no derivatives, and so does $z = |x| + |y|$ at the origin. Where what is inside an absolute value or a root vanishes, the calculator compares the value of f around it: if all are greater it is a minimum, if all are smaller a maximum, and if there are both, neither (like $|x| + y$, which has no extrema). It also warns about critical points that lie just outside the plotted range.
Donde $f_{x} = f_{y} = 0$ el plano tange: Where $f_{x} = f_{y} = 0$ the tangent plane is horizontal. With the Hessian $D = f_{xx} f_{yy} − f_{xy}^{2}$: if $D > 0$ and $f_{xx} > 0$ there is a minimum, if $D > 0$ and $f_{xx} < 0$ a maximum, if $D < 0$ a saddle point, and if $D = 0$ it cannot be decided this way.
Donde ∇f = 0, el hessiano D = fₓₓ·f_yy −: Where ∇f = 0, the Hessian D = fₓₓ·f_yy − fₓ_y² decides: D > 0 and fₓₓ > 0, minimum; D > 0 and fₓₓ < 0, maximum; D < 0, saddle point. For z = x² − y², D = −4 at the origin: saddle.
